newsitem.title: UK: Tomkins up on share buyback, profit in-line.
newsitem.headline: Tomkins up on share buyback, profit in-line.

text.p: Shares in British diversified group Tomkins Plc rose in pre-market trading on Monday after announcing a share buy back of up to 100 million stg, while its year profits were in line with estimates, traders said.
Shares were quoted 12-1/2p higher at 276-1/2p by 0727 GMT.
"It's up on the share buyback," one trader said.
Tomkins said its pre-tax profit for the year ending May 3 rose 33.7 percent to 431.8 million stg, in line with consensus estimates, and announced a 15 percent dividend increase.

Tomkins, an international group whose baking and specialised engineering activities include the British "Hovis" bread brand and Smith & Wesson handguns, said it was sitting on a cash pile of 617 million sterling ($1 billion).
The company said the current trading year was off to a good start, backed by "sound" orderbooks, and it was on course for further earnings and dividend growth.
